Both if it be M. and before whom are words of the rendering and are set in italic, as the edition sets renderings, and etc. stays roman as at GEN 30:27. Source wording is retained.

EZK 16:39 CCEL.why: Brenton’s θ caller stands before “thy proud ornaments” (1879 physical page 1013, 1900 physical page 1009, printed page 997), and the note glosses the whole noun phrase, τὰ σκεύη τῆς καυχήσεώς σου, as “the vessels or articles of thy glory”; “thy proud” alone is not what it renders.

DAG 7:16 CCEL.why: Brenton 1879 physical page 1077 and 1900 physical page 1073 (printed page 1061) print θ Or, certainty. with θ immediately before the first truth in “I sought to learn of him the truth of all these things”. The note glosses that noun alone, not him the.

DAG 9:25 CCEL.why: Brenton 1879 (physical page 1081, printed page 1065) and 1900 (physical page 1077, printed page 1065) print the caller immediately before 'seven weeks' and the note 'Or, sevens.' (footnote lettered δ against an in-text ζ, the plate's letters running one behind on that page); 1844 (vol. 2, physical page 374, printed page 871) sets '† Or, sevens.' at the same words. 'Sevens' renders ἑβδομάδες, the noun 'weeks', not the numeral ἑπτά, so 'seven' alone misstates the note; the caller begins the scope at 'seven', so the note is set on the phrase 'seven weeks', whose noun it glosses, with the source's words unchanged.

1CH 20:2 CCEL.why: CCEL 3.xx#3 reads A repetition. Brenton 1879 physical 571 and 1900 physical 567 (both printed 555) set the δ caller before their king; 1844 vol. 1 physical 479 (printed 455) sets its margin dagger before Molchom. Molchom and their king render the one Hebrew word twice, as Brenton's note at 2 Kingdoms 12:30 shows, and the printings disagree on which word is the repeat, so set the note on the whole doublet and leave out off his head.

HOS 3:4 CCEL.note: Gr. δήλων, Urim and Thummim probably meant, or rather Urim only.
HOS 3:4 CCEL.why: Brenton 1879 physical page 1088 and 1900 physical page 1084 (printed page 1072 in both) set only Gr. in italic; Urim and Thummim probably meant, or rather Urim only is the editor’s explanation of what δήλων refers to, not an alternative rendering of manifestations, so it stays roman, retaining all source words.

1KI 16:22.why: eBible sets the caller before the second followed (followed Thamni), but Brenton's μ stands before the first, followed Ambri, and the verse has no other caller (1879 physical p. 489, 1900 physical p. 485, printed p. 473); Gr. was after renders ὁ ὢν ὀπίσω Ἀμβρί, while the people that followed Thamni is τὸν ὀπίσω Θαμνί, without ὢν

ISA 19:2.why: Brenton 1844 vol. 2 physical p. 201 (printed p. 698), 1879 physical p. 869, 1884 physical p. 836 and 1900 physical p. 865 (printed p. 853 in the Bagster printings) set the same caller before both law words and print one Alex. ‘district,’ the accent being different note. Scope that single report to law against law, keeping his verse unchanged and completing both applications as district against district. Swete III p. 133 reads πόλις ἐπὶ πόλιν καὶ νομὸς ἐπὶ νομὸν and reports no A noun variant; retain the kept report and agrees:null rather than promote an unattested A accent reading.

EZK 8:10 CCEL.why: Brenton 1879 physical p. 1003 and 1900 physical p. 999 (printed p. 987) put ζ before them; Alex. αὐτοῦ reports the pronoun alone (ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῦ for the facing ἐπ᾽ αὐτοὺς), and κύκλῳ, round about, is common to both. Without English the clause rule would take round about into the lemma.

EZK 16:10 CCEL.why: Brenton’s alternative shod thee renders ὑπέδησα for the facing ὑπέδυσα, clothed thee beneath, whose beneath renders the prefix; it stands for the whole phrase. Widening the inferred lemma clothed thee echoed beneath into the alternative, printing shod thee beneath, which Brenton does not.

EZK 43:7 CCEL#2.why: Brenton 1879 physical p. 1055 and 1900 physical p. 1051 (printed p. 1039) print “Alex. κατασκηνώσει.” with γ immediately before shall dwell. The note gives a Greek verb with no English, so the explanatory rule would take in the following in the midst (ἐν μέσῳ), which the verb does not cover. Set it on shall dwell alone, which occurs once in the verse.

JOB 19:7 CCEL.why: Alex. λαλῶ (I speak) stands against γελῶ, which laugh renders; the report concerns that verb alone, not at reproach.

JOB 36:29 CCEL.why: Alex. ἐπέκτασιν is the noun outspreadings renders; of the clouds is not part of the reading.

JOB 42:8 CCEL.why: Alex. κάρπωμα is the noun burnt offering renders; for you is not part of the reading.

ECC 6:6 CCEL.note: Alex. begins the verse thus, Καὶ εἰ ἔζησε, _and if he has lived_, etc.
ECC 6:6 CCEL.why: Brenton reports how A opens the verse: begins the verse thus is his commentary, not a rendering, and the rendering is and if he has lived, his English of the Greek he quotes.

LEV 13:3.why: Brenton’s β stands before below, and lower than renders that one word; the skin follows in the gloss’s sense, not as its words.

LEV 13:3#2.why: Defile him renders the whole phrase pronounce him unclean (μιανεῖ αὐτόν), not its first two words.

LEV 13:12#2.why: According to the whole looking of the priest renders the whole clause, not its first words.

LEV 13:30.why: Brenton’s γ stands before beneath, and more hollow, lower than renders that one word.

LEV 13:31.why: Brenton 1900 physical p. 155 and 1879 physical p. 159 (printed p. 143) set δ before the first scurf, “the plague of the scurf”; Gr. breach renders that one, and the echo of and, behold would print words the note does not gloss.

LEV 14:15.why: The priest’s renders his own; left is the Greek’s too (τὴν ἀριστεράν).

LEV 16:32.why: Whosesoever hands they shall accomplish renders whomsoever they shall consecrate; to exercise the priestly office is the Greek’s next word (ἱερατεύειν).

1KI 14:1-20@6.why: The note ends with a complete explanatory sentence after its opening reading, so its final full stop stays.

1KI 14:1-20@12.why: The note ends with a complete explanatory sentence after its opening reading, so its final full stop stays.

1KI 14:1-20@omission1.why: The note explains the omitted passage in a complete sentence, so its final full stop stays.

PSA 67:16.why: Promote Brenton’s full literal gloss of the Septuagint’s τετυρωμένον, “curdled like cheese”, in place of his freer “swelling”; preserve the former rendering in the same source note. This is an alternative translation of the same Greek, not a reading from another witness.
